summary: The narrator, Rio, and Checker discover that all electronics have failed, which Rio and Checker attribute to an EMP attack, most likely a high-altitude nuclear detonation. A battery-powered radio in a Faraday cage reports a localized event affecting Southern California, parts of Arizona and Nevada, and Mexico, with FEMA and the National Guard deploying. Rio concludes the blackout is a stalling tactic to let the attackers hunt them down, and the scene ends with the narrator asking what to do.
one_line: After an EMP knocks out all electronics in Southern California, the characters hear a radio report and realize the blackout is a stalling tactic by their pursuers.
key_facts: Rio pulled the burner cell out of his pocket, reinserted the battery, and pressed the power button, and nothing happened.
Rio said, "Not a power outage" and attributed the failure to an EMP attack.
Rio said Pithica was warned by the alerts going out and was protecting itself.
Checker said a high-altitude nuclear detonation is probably the easiest way to produce an EMP.
Checker said one high-altitude nuke could take out all the electronics in the United States.
Checker said there would be no loss of human life, except for people depending on medical electronics.
The narrator asked about cars, and Checker said most cars are computerized these days and older ones might have a better chance.
Checker had been backing up in the cloud, and the narrator asked whether the network would still work from a place that was not fried.
Rio found a working radio kept inside a metal box in a Faraday cage, which a survivalist had stored.
A radio broadcast said it was unverified whether the event was an attack or a natural phenomenon.
The President asked people to help each other and avoid panic, and FEMA and the National Guard were being deployed to affected areas.
The event was at least localized to Southern California and parts of Arizona, Nevada, and Mexico.
Rio said, "This is not their endgame," and the narrator agreed it was a stalling tactic.
Rio said the attackers would have some plan of escalation and were very efficient when they pooled their resources.
Checker's voice had gone very high when he wondered whether they had taken out the whole country.
